title: 26.1: A 24GHz Direct Digital Transmitter Using Multiphase Subharmonic Switching PA Achieving 3.2Gb/s Data Rate and -30.8dB EVM in 65nm CMOS
problem: Wide-bandwidth (multi-Gb/s) RF transmitters for K/Ka-band (24GHz) must achieve low EVM and high efficiency across peak and back-off power levels, but IQ summation causes 3dB power loss and prior subharmonic switching (SHS) designs were bandwidth-limited to tens of MHz.
method: Multiphase subharmonic switching (MP-SHS) transmitter architecture combines phase-shifted subharmonic LO divider (attenuating subharmonic spurs via phase shift), current-shared phase-interpolator MUX for MP LO generation, and dual-rate hybrid DAC with noise shaping to enable 3.2Gb/s operation at 24GHz while maintaining peak and PBO efficiency.

title: RTSpMSpM: Harnessing Ray Tracing for Efficient Sparse Matrix Computations
problem: Sparse matrix-matrix multiplication (SpMSpM) is a critical kernel for graph analytics, GNNs, and scientific computing, but existing GPU SpMSpM libraries underutilize hardware because the irregular memory access and conditional computation patterns of sparse data do not map well to standard GPU CUDA cores and tensor units.
method: The authors first observe the algorithmic analogy between SpMSpM (identifying non-zero output positions) and ray-triangle intersection (finding ray-geometry intersections), then implement SW-RTSpMSpM — an SpMSpM algorithm mapped to the standard ray tracing API (DXR/OptiX) that uses RT core intersection units for non-zero position detection. Analysis of the differences between the two algorithms motivates RT+SpMSpM, which introduces two architectural optimizations: (1) simultaneous computation of partial products alongside RT intersection tests (not just detection), and (2) a ray mapping and scheduling strategy paired with a small row accumulation engine (RAE) that exploits Gustavson's sparse row-by-column dataflow and eliminates reliance on shader fallbacks and redundant memory operations. The RAE introduces only 0.2% area overhead on a modern high-end RT GPU.

title: An Input-Aware Sparse Tensor Compiler Empowered by Vectorized Acceleration
problem: Sparse tensor computations (especially sparse matrix-matrix multiplication) suffer from poor performance due to rigid sparse formats and limited compiler support for diverse sparsity patterns. Existing tensor compilers offer limited sparse optimizations, forcing practitioners to choose between manual kernel design (high effort) and generic code generation (suboptimal performance).
method: SpMMTC analyzes the non-zero distribution of input sparse matrices at compile time and generates vectorized kernels optimized for the specific sparsity pattern. The compiler adapts to hardware ISA capabilities (SIMD width, cache hierarchy) and creates specialized SpMM kernels without manual tuning. Vectorization guidance and pattern-aware unrolling maximize hardware utilization.

title: QuCLEAR: Clifford Extraction and Absorption for Quantum Circuit Optimization
problem: Near-term quantum devices have high gate error rates, and the dominant approach of reducing two-qubit gate count via peephole optimization or routing-aware compilation leaves substantial overhead from Clifford subcircuits that could be eliminated rather than merely rearranged.
method: QuCLEAR is a compilation framework with two sequential optimization steps. First, Clifford Extraction identifies and extracts Clifford subcircuits from the original circuit, commuting them to the end of the circuit via a series of gate commutation rules while simultaneously optimizing (reducing) the remaining non-Clifford gates; this process changes the structure of the remaining circuit to expose further simplifications. Second, Clifford Absorption leverages the classical simulatability of Clifford circuits to compute their effect analytically and absorb (classically post-process) the extracted Clifford subcircuit rather than executing it on quantum hardware, eliminating those gates entirely from the quantum circuit.

title: Late Breaking Results: Advanced PCB Placement with Irregular Components for Efficient Collision Detection and Routability Optimization
problem: Automated PCB placement must handle heterogeneous components with irregular geometries and complex design rules while ensuring collision-free placement and routability.
method: Three-stage placement framework: (1) global placement with Separating Axis Theorem for collision detection on exact component contours and board shapes, (2) multi-stage force-directed method dynamically adjusting attractive/repulsive forces for clearance and routability, (3) scanline-based legalization resolving overlaps and enforcing spacing constraints. Framework adapts to diverse design limitations.

title: MEGA.mini: A NPU with Novel Heterogeneous AI Processing Architecture Balancing Efficiency, Performance, and Intelligence for the Era of Generative AI
problem: AI accelerators must balance low-precision compute efficiency against accuracy preservation for outlier values; MEGA.mini proposes a heterogeneous NPU architecture supporting both fixed-point and floating-point computation dynamically.
method: MEGA.mini combines a large fixed-point compute fabric (FXP, >95% operations) with a smaller floating-point unit handling outlier values (<5%), using a big.LITTLE heterogeneous core design that switches between execution modes based on data characteristics. Three hierarchical solutions (MEGA, median, mini) scale across deployment targets.

title: LeakyDSP: Exploiting Digital Signal Processing Blocks to Sense Voltage Fluctuations in FPGAs
problem: Cloud FPGA multi-tenancy enables power side-channel attacks; existing attacks rely on crafted circuits, but DSP blocks—abundant in modern FPGAs—remain unexploited as malicious sensors.
method: Proposes LeakyDSP, a malicious configuration of DSP blocks to sense fine-grained voltage fluctuations in FPGAs; DSP blocks are reconfigured as voltage sensors to detect colocated circuit activity and extract secrets.

title: The Crucial Role of Semiconductors in the Software-Defined Vehicle
problem: Modern vehicles require software-defined architectures to meet emission standards, enable intelligent connectivity, and support sustainable mobility—demanding advanced semiconductor solutions.
method: Position paper outlining the semiconductor technology roadmap and system requirements to enable software-defined vehicle architectures with central compute, over-the-air updates, and intelligent edge processing.

title: 2.8: A 210fps Image Signal Processor for 4K Ultra HD True Video Super Resolution
problem: Conventional video super-resolution treats frames as independent images, neglecting temporal and spatial redundancies in video encoding (I/P/B frames, block prediction, residuals), resulting in inefficient computation and high energy cost.
method: A dedicated video super-resolution ISP leverages inter-frame dependencies and video codec structure. The processor exploits temporal redundancy by reusing features from adjacent frames and spatial redundancy by utilizing residual/motion vector information from codec blocks. Multi-frame alignment and refinement stages process P/B frames referencing previous/future frames, incorporating motion vectors and residuals directly into the VSR pipeline rather than treating video as raw frames.

title: Presto: A Unified RISC-V-Compatible SoC for Multi-Scheme FHE Acceleration over Module Lattice
problem: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) enables computation on encrypted data but incurs orders of magnitude computational overhead; software FHE is impractical for latency-sensitive applications.
method: Presto integrates a RISC-V core with specialized hardware accelerators for polynomial operations (NTT, convolution) and module lattice arithmetic. It supports multiple FHE schemes (BGV, CKKS) through flexible dataflow and instruction extensions.

title: SparseWeaver: Converting Sparse Operations as Dense Operations on GPUs for Graph Workloads
problem: Real-world graph workloads have sparse and skewed adjacency structures that cause severe warp-level load imbalance on GPUs, where existing software or hardware balancing schemes incur memory overhead or excessive inter- and intra-warp synchronization cost.
method: SparseWeaver is a hardware-software co-design that converts sparse graph operations into balanced dense operations by exploiting graph topology. A lightweight GPU functional unit microarchitecture called Weaver is added to GPU cores; it analyzes common sparse-to-dense conversion patterns identified via static/dynamic analysis and implements the conversion directly in the execution pipeline, leveraging memory access locality without additional synchronization. The design is prototyped on the open-source RISC-V Vortex GPU.

title: A 1Tb 3b/cell 3D-Flash Memory with a 29%-Improved-Energy-Efficiency Read Operation and 4.8Gb/s Power-Isolated Low-Tapped-Termination I/Os
problem: 3D Flash memory for AI applications requires high-speed I/O and energy-efficient reads; reducing circuit overhang from the memory array (in CMOS-bonded-array or CMOS-under-array designs) limits chip area, while energy efficiency is critical for large-scale deployments.
method: 1Tb 3D Flash memory in 3b/cell technology with: (1) 29% improved energy-efficient read operation via small-voltage-swing word-line (WL) control, (2) 4.8Gb/s power-isolated low-tapped-termination I/Os that minimize circuit overhang beyond the memory array.

title: A 50Gb/s Burst-Mode NRZ Receiver with 5-Tap FFE, 7-Tap DFE and 15ns Lock Time in 28nm CMOS for Symmetric 50G-PON
problem: 50G PON receivers face severe inter-symbol interference (ISI) from chromatic dispersion and limited photonic bandwidth; burst-mode operation requires rapid lock (<15ns) with high SNR tolerance. Existing designs trade fast lock for equalization depth (1-tap DFE insufficient for 50G).
method: A burst-mode receiver in 28nm CMOS integrates 5-tap FFE (3 pre, 1 post) and 7-tap DFE (4 floating post-cursors up to 16th tap) for deep ISI cancellation. Edge equalization with fast-lock circuitry achieves 15ns lock time while APD integration supports standard-defined high-gain photodiode operation.

title: Exo 2: Growing a Scheduling Language
problem: User-schedulable languages (USLs) fix a single design point for what programmers control and what is automated, but no universal control/automation split exists even in narrow domains, causing USLs to be inextensible when new hardware targets or optimization strategies emerge.
method: Exo 2 enables users to define new scheduling operations externally to the compiler by composing a set of trusted fine-grained primitives (actions for modifying code, inspection for querying code structure, and references for pointing to code locations). The key mechanism is Cursors, a new abstraction that unifies code references across actions, inspections, and scheduling library composition, allowing safe user-defined scheduling transformations. Users build scheduling libraries that amortize transformation effort across related kernels without modifying the compiler internals.

title: PipeLink: A Pipelined Resource Sharing System for Dataflow High-Level Synthesis
problem: Dynamically scheduled HLS produces pipelined dataflow circuits, but coordinating pipelined function calls and shared resources is difficult without centralized control, limiting support for general software programs.
method: PipeLink decomposes synthesis into compilation and linking stages, enabling fully-pipelined access to shared functions in asynchronous dataflow circuits. Uses asynchronous design principles for both pipelined function units and pipelined memory access in a unified framework.

title: Scaling Laws of Graph Neural Networks for Atomistic Materials Modeling
problem: GNNs for atomistic materials modeling remain small (millions of parameters) compared to LLMs (billions); lack of scaling guidance limits accuracy and applicability to complex materials discovery tasks.
method: Develops foundational GNN with billions of parameters trained on terabyte-scale datasets; incorporates LLM-inspired training techniques (efficient data/model management) to enable large-scale GNN training and deployment; explores three scaling dimensions: architecture, dataset size, and training method applicability.
